task: Add the save-time contract API surface (platform flag, contract_validation issue fields, coverage object, all-errors-at-once rejection, create/update/dry-run parity and a new validate-before-first-save endpoint) to the workflow save/dry-run pipeline.

key_reasoning.reason: Touches the workflow router (create, update, dry-run, response models, error envelope, new endpoint), WorkflowService.validate_for_update and the version service, the WorkflowExecutor stage sequence, the contracts linker/models/policy, validation models and line_lookup, and Config. The report currently never reaches the routers, so a new carrier abstraction is needed. Single repo.

The technical analysis lists several ticket-vs-code contradictions: path and details semantics differ from the linker output, the config_path table does not match the linker's record paths and omits task and config.input_key, the warning kind is misnamed, UNVERIFIED records are info rather than warning, and 'both dry-run shapes' is undefined. Design decisions are open, with rework risk.

The closest pattern is the existing kind-keyed warnings and structured error dicts. It does not cover a structured carrier for warnings and coverage when error_format=string, or the authorization rules of the new unsaved-workflow endpoint (project read access only, with no stored workflow for the global/marketplace/guardrail checks). Create, update and dry-run diverge today in parse failure handling, model-id normalization and MCP checks. 13 validate_workflow callers are exposed to any default change. Several enumerated edge cases (UNVERIFIED, rejected-save coverage with failure_report zero counts) have no covering test template. Authorization red flag applied.

About 8-10 source files modified (routers/workflow.py, workflows/workflow.py, contracts/linker.py, contracts/models.py, validation/models.py, line_lookup.py, workflow_service.py, workflow_version_service.py, configs/config.py), 1-2 new, plus router, linker and parity tests across 3+ directories.
